title: Recovery

learn.summary: Training is the stimulus; recovery is where adaptation actually happens. Sleep is the single most powerful recovery tool — studies show sleeping under 6 hours can cut muscle protein synthesis and double injury rates in athletes. If you're chronically under-recovered, more training makes you worse, not better.

do: Set a phone alarm for bedtime (not just wake-up) tonight, placed to give you a realistic 7.5–8 hours in bed.

children.title: Sleep as Recovery

learn.summary: Growth hormone pulses during deep sleep do much of your rebuilding; adults training regularly do best on 7–9 hours. The highest-leverage habits are boring: consistent wake time (even weekends), dark cool room around 18°C (65°F), and no caffeine within 8 hours of bed. One study of basketball players extending sleep to 10 hours improved sprint times and shooting accuracy within weeks.

do: Track your in-bed and wake times for 7 days and calculate your true average sleep — most people overestimate by 30–60 minutes.

children.title: Rest Days

learn.summary: Muscles typically need 48–72 hours to fully recover from hard training, which is why full-body programs run 3 days a week with days between. A rest day is not a nothing day — walking, easy cycling, and mobility work speed recovery by increasing blood flow without adding damage. Guard at least one true low-intensity day per week permanently.

do: Designate your rest days for the next two weeks in advance and plan a 20-minute walk on each one.

children.title: Soreness vs Injury

learn.summary: DOMS is dull, symmetrical, muscle-belly soreness peaking 24–72 hours after novel exercise and easing with movement — annoying but harmless. Injury signals are different: sharp or stabbing pain, pain at a joint or tendon, one-sided pain, swelling, or pain that worsens as you warm up. The first kind you train through gently; the second you stop for and get assessed if it persists past a week.

do: Next time something hurts, run the checklist before training: sharp vs dull, joint vs muscle, one side vs both, better or worse with warm-up — and act accordingly.

children.title: Active Recovery

learn.summary: Light movement clears soreness faster than total rest: 20–30 minutes of walking, easy swimming, or gentle cycling at a heart rate under about 60% of max increases circulation without new fatigue. Contrast showers, saunas, and massage guns are fine but minor — they're the garnish, not the meal. The meal is sleep, food, and easy movement.

do: The day after your hardest session this week, do 20 minutes of deliberately easy movement instead of nothing — note how the soreness compares to usual.
